content:
nina: kicking off bluejay-11b (int4) canary in pool-lowlat. will run the usual smoke + evals. leaving batch settings as-is for the first run.
sam: quick heads up: our date-parse eval EM fell from 0.86 -> 0.80 after the int4 artifacts. consistent across runs.
jordan: seeing intermittent OOMs under load on two machines. logs show heavy slab fragmentation + repeated small frees.
eva: repro steps: single long-gen with max_new_tokens=1200 and microbatch=3 triggers OOM in ~10-20 tokens. runtime excerpt: ```WARN slab: free_list empty; alloc_retry=3; gc_cycles=89; failed_alloc=allocate_kv_page(24576000)```
nina: bluejay tokenization tends to expand some dates into longer sequences, so effective seq len is higher than we planned. that could cause big kv allocations and fragmentation.
sam: digging into quality: int4 mapping used a uniform per-layer clip. suspect skew at LN-adjacent layers causing output drift.
jordan: rough theory: quant-induced changes increase attention footprint per token -> more kv writes -> more small allocations -> freelist thrash -> allocator falls back to slow path which can drop or delay kv writes, causing occasional token instability.
eva: observed token mismatch patterns: low-confidence tokens replaced by <unk-like> or short spaces when failures occurred. timing-sensitive.
sam: suggested mitigation plan: (A) lower default max_new_tokens to 512 for the int4 canary, (B) enable kv_warmup on first request to pre-alloc N pages, (C) tweak per-layer clip for layers near LN, regenerate int4 artifacts, (D) limit microbatch concurrency to 5 per GPU.
nina: +1 on reducing defaults. most product flows under 512.
jordan: runtime change I can land: deferred_free_bucket (per-thread reserve) to smooth free churn; behind a config flag for canary. should lower global freelist contention.
eva: example canary config to try: ```model: bluejay-11b
variant: int4
quant_clip_map: {ln_post: 0.005, att_out: 0.007}
defaults: {max_new_tokens: 512, microbatch_limit: 5, kv_warmup: true, deferred_free_bucket: true}```
ops-bot: enqueue canary deploy: deploy/bluejay-11b-int4 -> pool-lowlat-04 by nina @ 1990010200
deploy-bot: canary liveliness OK after 6m, perf: p50 +2ms, p95 +9ms; rss -16% vs int8; allocator_fragmentation (slab_free_ratio) down marginally after deferred_free_bucket.
sam: re-run evals after config+clip tweak: date-parse EM = 0.84 on int4 (was 0.80) 11 still -0.02 vs int8 but within our rollback threshold. quality regression largely mitigated.
jordan: 48h soak under synthetic ramp (concurrency up to 6): no OOMs, slab_gc_cycles down ~6x, tail microspikes reduced to <0.1% of requests.
eva: suggest adding a token-stability CI for onboarding: measures token-flip rate under tight timing and repeated seeds. quick command: 
```bash
./ci/evals/run_token_stability_2.sh --model bluejay-11b --variant int4 --iters 40 --suite date-parse
```
logs -> /evals/runs/1990010000-tokenstab.log
nina: actions: sam to finalize per-layer clip_map + regen int4 (ETA ~3h), jordan to land deferred_free_bucket behind flag (ETA ~2h), ops to flip max_new_tokens->512 and kv_warmup for bluejay canary (done), eva to add token-stability CI (ETA tomorrow morning).
sam: will add a clear note in the model-catalog: "bluejay-11b int4: requires reduced max_new_tokens and kv_warmup; see allocator notes".
jordan: longer-term if we need 1k+ token support we should explore dynamic_kv_page or transient reservation to avoid huge single-shot allocations.
nina: good work. we'll monitor the canary metrics and run the token-stability suite. escalate if EM drifts.
